newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq to delist Voice Powered shares.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq to delist Voice Powered shares.

text.p: Voice Powered Technology International Inc said the National Association of Securities Dealers (NASD) denied the company's appeal to keep listing its securities on the Nasdaq SmallCap Market.
Effective April 9, Voice Powered shares would be delisted and would instead be eligible to trade on the OTC Bulletin Board, it said.
Voice Powered also said Ernest Townsend, a director since 1994, resigned due to personal commitments that would have limited his availability to the company.
Voice Powered, which was not immediately available to comment further, designs, develops and markets low cost, portable voice recognition consumer electronics products.

On February 14, the company said its shares might face delisting on the NASDAQ Small Cap system. The company said it had until February 26 to meet listing requirements or submit a proposal for achieving compliance.

Voice Powered said then it had a proposal which included a reverse stock split which should raise its share price above the NASD minimum requirement of $1 per share, assuming financing commitments were obtained in time.
